extracted.intended_audience: industry partners, donors, faculty, prospective students, and research collaborators
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional overview of Penn State's research enterprise describing priorities, scale, partnership modalities, and opportunities for engagement. Intended to inform industry partners, donors, students, and collaborators about how to work with Penn State and what metrics and offerings characterize the enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on long-term research impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Penn State Research is dedicated to the 'long game' of research across our enterprise, focused on impact and not only on scientific results or publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate success by visible changes in communities, global health, economic wellness, humanitarian efforts and worldwide positioning over many years, not solely by publications or short-term scientific results. (Quote: 'It’s time to understand the true impact of our research enterprise.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity as a core quality
rubrics_metrics.description: We are an interdisciplinary research powerhouse enabled through eight interdisciplinary research institutes, the Applied Research Laboratory, and 18 colleges performing research from STEM to the arts, law, and communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to work that leverages cross-college and cross-institute collaboration; interdisciplinary scope and use of institutional research centers and labs are indicators of strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and resource metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional scale is communicated via research expenditures and counts: '$1.44 Billion 2024-2025 Research Expenditures', 'Ranked 25 Nationwide for Research Expenditures', '2000+ Industry Partnerships in the last decade', '9000+ Industry Research Projects since 2013.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these measurable indicators (annual expenditures, national ranking, number of partnerships and projects) as signals of capacity, stability, and experience when evaluating Penn State as a partner or grant recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership engagement modalities (Involvement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many ways to work together including: Research, Co-development of projects and grants, Internships & Co-ops, Student Training Programs, Talent Pipeline Program, Centers of Excellence, Commercialization Opportunities, License Technology, Research Park and Incubation Facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing collaboration, map your needs to one or more of these engagement types; successful partnerships typically choose modalities that align with workforce development, commercialization, or joint research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Support services available: Core Facilities, Student Consultant, Hardware Grants, Curriculum Development, Workshops/Seminars, Student Organization Sponsorship, Student Mentorships, Guest Speakers/Lecturers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage institutional support to supplement project capacity; proposals or collaboration requests should specify which support offerings are sought and how they advance project outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsorship avenues include: Research projects, New ventures, Seed and venture funds, Joint initiatives, Student fellowships and scholarships, Research consortiums, Innovative facilities and equipment, Outreach programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors can target student training, research scaling, or venture support; specify desired sponsorship outcomes (e.g., fellowships, equipment, consortium membership) to align donor resources with institutional programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic partner benefits and collaboration goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic partnership elements: Cooperative business development, Workforce development strategies, Joint education-focused legislative petitioning, Endowments and legacy opportunities, Expanded talent pipeline, New Commercialization Opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic partners should articulate long-term objectives (workforce, commercialization, policy/advocacy, endowment) and propose cooperative models that integrate these elements with Penn State's programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student involvement and training as an impact metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and creative inquiry opportunities exist in every discipline and in every year of academic study; student involvement is a highlighted outcome ('Tomorrow’s brightest minds are working in Penn State research today').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess projects in part by their capacity to provide student research experiences, internships, and career preparation; proposals emphasizing student training and pipelines are aligned with institutional priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of philanthropy in advancing research
rubrics_metrics.description: Gifts support research in varied forms—from online contributions to in-kind donations and estate gifts—cultivating curiosity across institutes, colleges, and campuses. Examples include endowed institutes and named professorships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philanthropic contributions can be structured to launch institutes, endow faculty positions, or fund specific labs or programs; donors and grant-seekers should outline how gifts will translate to research capacity and impact.
